description: Single source for architecture arrows, flow messages, code references, language and deployment. Generated assets must not be edited by hand.

components.name: Customer / operations UI
components.scaling: No background polling. Bounded API lists, manual refresh.

components.name: Chargeback API
components.scaling: Replicate stateless API pods; bounded request body and PostgreSQL connection pool.

components.name: PostgreSQL + work queue
components.scaling: Four logical partitions; eligibility and due-work indexes. Physical sharding is not implemented. Managed cloud PostgreSQL is proposed, not provisioned.

components.name: Four daily slots
components.scaling: 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC. Replays share durable slot and assignment records.

components.name: Claim and build CSV
components.scaling: Up to BATCH_MAX_ROWS rows per file and SCHEDULE_MAX_BATCHES per run. Advisory lock bounds active schedulers.

components.name: CSV artifact storage
components.scaling: Objects have stable batch-derived keys; files are bounded at 10,000 rows / 4 MiB. Local provider: SeaweedFS. Cloud object storage is proposed, not provisioned.

components.name: Delivery worker
components.scaling: Bounded due-work query and one active transfer per process. Scale replicas with a per-batch advisory lock.

components.name: Visa / Mastercard simulator
components.scaling: One receiver with persistent volume and SQLite receipts. This is a simulator, not card-network certification.

flows.name: Create a chargeback
flows.note: Synthetic imported transactions and provisioned, expiring tokens keep scope small. There is no card-number intake or identity-provider integration.

messages.label: Submit the dispute
messages.request:
POST /api/chargebacks
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: <stable UUID>
{"transaction_id":"UUID","amount_minor":"1250","reason":"FRAUD"}
messages.request_label: POST /api/chargebacks + Idempotency-Key
messages.explanation: The UI retains the key while a submission has an uncertain response. Amounts stay decimal strings at the HTTP boundary; Go parses an exact signed 64-bit integer.
messages.simplification: Customer UI keeps a retry key only while this page remains open. One chargeback per transaction still prevents duplicates after a reload.

messages.label: Authorize the customer
messages.request: SELECT customer_id, role FROM tokens WHERE hash = SHA256(bearer token), not revoked and not expired
messages.response: Customer principal, or HTTP 401/403
messages.request_label: Bearer token → active token lookup
messages.explanation: The database owns customer identity. Tokens are hashed at rest and never placed in a URL or browser storage.

messages.label: Commit intake and its audit event
messages.request: BEGIN; validate transaction ownership and amount; INSERT chargebacks ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; COMMIT
messages.response: Inserted ID or existing idempotent result after commit
messages.request_label: INSERT chargeback + unique customer/key + transaction
messages.explanation: The database enforces one chargeback per transaction and one request per customer/key. Concurrent losers read the winner. A trigger writes the acceptance audit event in the same transaction.
messages.durable: Chargeback accepted + append-only audit event; partition fixed for life
messages.simplification: Partitions spread claim work logically within one PostgreSQL database; they are not physical shards.

flows.name: Read customer status
flows.note: Lists are bounded to the most recent 100 records. This first version does not yet provide cursor pagination.

messages.label: Read owned transactions and chargebacks
messages.request:
GET /api/transactions
GET /api/chargebacks
GET /api/chargebacks/{id}
Authorization: Bearer <customer token>
messages.request_label: GET transactions / chargebacks / chargeback ID
messages.explanation: A customer sees only their imported transactions and chargebacks. The UI refreshes from the real API, not a local model.

messages.label: Join immutable assignment to batch state
messages.request: SELECT owned chargeback JOIN transaction LEFT JOIN batch WHERE chargeback.customer_id = authenticated customer
messages.response: Chargeback fields and COALESCE(batch.state, pending)
messages.request_label: SELECT with customer ownership predicate
messages.explanation: Status comes directly from durable assignment and delivery state. A missing acknowledgement remains submitted or unknown, never acknowledged.

flows.name: Schedule a six-hour slot
flows.note: Kubernetes CronJob is the scheduler. Missed slots can be replayed explicitly. Each run is bounded; an unfinished slot needs another run.

messages.label: Launch bounded slot work
messages.request:
Cron schedule: 0 */6 * * *; timeZone: Etc/UTC
Run nexo schedule [--cutoff <six-hour UTC boundary>]
messages.response: Process exit and {claimed: integer, built: integer, complete: boolean} or {busy: true, claimed: 0, built: 0}
messages.request_label: 00, 06, 12, 18 UTC → schedule Job
messages.response_label: Job exits; counts and completion status
messages.explanation: The cutoff is a six-hour UTC boundary. Rows committed too late for one scan remain unassigned and are eligible in a later slot.
messages.simplification: A small single active scheduler makes the learning path clear. Durable row claiming remains the correctness boundary.

messages.label: Persist the slot and recover unfinished batches
messages.request: pg_try_advisory_lock(817203, 1); INSERT slots(cutoff) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; SELECT building batches LIMIT schedule_max_batches
messages.response: Exclusive scheduler ownership; existing slot and bounded recovery list
messages.request_label: INSERT slot; list unfinished building batches
messages.response_label: Existing or new durable slot; recovery batch IDs
messages.explanation: Replaying a slot never resets membership. Unfinished file generation is resumed before new claims.
messages.durable: Slot exists; building batches retain their original members

flows.name: Claim rows and build a CSV
flows.note: CSV uses an explicit simulator contract, not a proprietary Visa/Mastercard file specification. Bounded memory holds at most one file.

messages.label: Claim eligible rows once
messages.protocol: psycopg transaction / FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
messages.request: SELECT unassigned chargebacks received before cutoff, filtered by network + partition, LIMIT batch_max_rows FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; INSERT batch; UPDATE batch_id; COMMIT
messages.response: Batch UUID and permanently assigned members, or no eligible rows
messages.request_label: SELECT … FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + assign batch_id
messages.explanation: Locking lets one claimant take a row. Assignment and the batch are committed together. Database triggers reject changing an assigned batch or its financial fields.
messages.durable: Unassigned chargebacks → permanent batch membership; building batch created

messages.label: Serialize deterministic CSV and store it
messages.request:
PutObject(Bucket, Key="exports/{network}/{slot}/{batch_id}.csv", Body=<UTF-8 CSV>, Metadata={sha256,batch-id})
Header: chargeback_id,transaction_id,network,currency,amount_minor,reason
Rows sorted by chargeback ID; CRLF line endings
messages.response: S3 successful object write, or exception; generation retries use same key and exact bytes
messages.request_label: PutObject: deterministic CSV + SHA-256 metadata
messages.explanation: Exact integer strings are serialized in a stable order. A crash after storage and before the database commit can only regenerate this batch, never new membership.
messages.simplification: Application identity and digest checks protect the artifact. Object-lock retention and a certified card-network format are outside this deployment.

messages.label: Commit the file manifest
messages.request: UPDATE batches SET state=ready, object_key, sha256, byte_count; INSERT file_ready audit event; COMMIT
messages.response: Committed manifest available to delivery workers
messages.request_label: UPDATE ready + object key / digest / size
messages.response_label: COMMIT; ready work visible to worker poll
messages.explanation: The worker cannot discover ready work until the manifest transaction commits. Database triggers prevent the artifact identity changing after building.
messages.durable: building → ready with immutable file manifest and audit event

flows.name: Deliver one file
flows.note: SFTP encrypts file transfer but does not provide exactly-once processing. Permanent assignment, one filename, durable publication intent and receiver deduplication supply separate guarantees.

messages.label: Poll durable work and own one batch
messages.request: SELECT ready, unknown, submitted batches due now LIMIT 20; pg_try_advisory_lock(batch ID); INSERT delivery_attempts
messages.response: Exclusive batch ownership and durable attempt UUID, or already owned
messages.request_label: Poll due batches, lock one, record attempt
messages.explanation: A process holds a session advisory lock while it handles one batch. A dead worker releases the lock; the next owner records its old attempt as interrupted.
messages.durable: Delivery attempt recorded before external I/O

messages.label: Read and verify the immutable artifact
messages.request: GetObject(Bucket, Key from database manifest), read at most 4 MiB + 1 byte
messages.response: CSV bytes with exact byte count and SHA-256, or integrity conflict
messages.request_label: GetObject for stored object key
messages.explanation: The delivery worker compares bytes against the durable database manifest rather than trusting object metadata.

messages.label: Open a pinned SSH session and upload temporary bytes
messages.request: Connect using known_hosts host-key verification; OpenFile(/incoming/.{batch_id}.{attempt_id}.tmp, WRONLY|CREATE|EXCL); copy bytes; close; read back
messages.response: Verified temporary file, or bounded transport/integrity error
messages.request_label: SSH host-key check; write unique .tmp; read back
messages.explanation: The receiver ignores temporary files. Interrupted writes can be retried using a new attempt filename before publication intent exists.
messages.simplification: Simulator authentication uses a generated password. Production bank transport identity and key rotation need separate integration.

messages.label: Commit publication intent before rename
messages.request: UPDATE batches SET publication_started=true, state=unknown WHERE id=$1 AND state=ready AND NOT publication_started; audit trigger writes publication_intent in same commit
messages.response: Exactly one changed row; publication fence is permanent
messages.request_label: COMMIT publication_started=true, state=unknown + audit
messages.explanation: Once this flag may be committed, any uncertain upload outcome must be reconciled. Absence of a final file is no longer permission to publish again.
messages.durable: ready → unknown; permanent publication intent + audit event commit together

messages.label: Publish one final filename
messages.request: Rename(/incoming/.{batch_id}.{attempt_id}.tmp, /incoming/{batch_id}.csv), without replacement
messages.response: Success, already-exists error or lost response; reconcile final file and acknowledgement; a verified final file changes unknown to submitted
messages.request_label: Rename .tmp → {batch_id}.csv; never overwrite
messages.explanation: The receiver exposes a complete immutable final file with an atomic no-replace operation. The final name is derived from the permanent batch ID.
messages.durable: Receiver final file becomes durable before success response
messages.simplification: No-replace durable publication is explicitly part of this simulator contract. Real partner SFTP capabilities and retention must be agreed before integration.

flows.name: Reconcile an ambiguous delivery
flows.note: Safety takes priority over automatic progress. If publication started and both final file and acknowledgement are absent, the batch stays unknown and needs receiver evidence; it is not republished. Once a final file was verified, later absence or transport failure preserves submitted; acknowledgement is still required.

messages.label: Read acknowledgement, then final file
messages.request: Read /acks/{batch_id}.json first; if absent, read /incoming/{batch_id}.csv; compare identity, digest, row count and size
messages.response: Matching ACK → acknowledged/rejected; matching final → submitted; mismatch → conflict; absent after intent → unknown; previously verified submitted status is preserved on later absence
messages.request_label: Read ACK first; otherwise verify final CSV
messages.explanation: A timeout can hide a successful rename. Checking the same identity recovers known outcomes without inventing another file. Missing evidence is preserved as unknown. A later outage cannot erase an earlier verified submission.

messages.label: Persist outcome and schedule another check
messages.request: UPDATE batch state, acknowledgement, safe last_error, next_attempt_at; UPDATE delivery_attempt outcome; COMMIT
messages.response: Durable status and attempt; next due check in 30 seconds for nonterminal work
messages.request_label: UPDATE outcome + delivery attempt + next check
messages.explanation: Delivery status and the attempt result commit together. Unknown is observable in the operations view and is never converted to success by a timer.
messages.durable: ready / unknown / submitted → reconciled state and completed attempt

flows.name: Receiver acknowledgement
flows.note: The simulator stores its own receipt ledger and can inject rejection, delayed or missing acknowledgements, partial uploads, timeouts and disconnect after rename.

messages.label: Receiver ingests the published CSV
messages.request: Scan final .csv only; validate header, UUIDs, network, integer amount and reason; INSERT receipt and unique chargeback membership
messages.response: Durable accepted or rejected receipt, deduplicated by batch ID and chargeback ID
messages.request_label: Background scan of final CSV → validate and deduplicate
messages.explanation: SQLite transactions are the receiver-side processing boundary. A chargeback ID already recorded from another file rejects the new file.
messages.durable: Receiver receipt + unique chargeback membership committed
messages.simplification: The simulator ledger is deliberately separate from Nexo PostgreSQL and is not a real card-network decision system.

messages.label: Write durable acknowledgement JSON
messages.request:
Write /acks/{batch_id}.json via temporary file
{"version":1,"batch_id":"UUID","sha256":"64 lowercase hex","row_count":1,"status":"accepted|rejected","reason":null}
messages.response: Complete JSON acknowledgement visible via SFTP; delayed or missing in fault modes
messages.request_label: Receipt → temporary ACK → fsync + atomic rename
messages.explanation: Acknowledgements identify the exact bytes and number of rows. Missing acknowledgements remain pending on the Nexo side.

messages.label: Validate receiver evidence
messages.request: GET /acks/{batch_id}.json; strict JSON fields; expected version=1, batch ID, SHA-256, row_count, accepted/rejected status
messages.response: Validated acknowledgement, absent file, or conflict
messages.request_label: Read and validate exact acknowledgement contract
messages.explanation: A receipt is trusted only when its batch identity and file manifest match. Rejection is a terminal outcome, not a trigger to assign chargebacks again.

messages.label: Commit acknowledged or rejected
messages.request: UPDATE batch state acknowledged|rejected and acknowledgement JSON; complete delivery attempt; COMMIT
messages.response: Terminal batch state visible to customer and operations
messages.request_label: UPDATE terminal state + acknowledgement + attempt
messages.response_label: COMMIT; terminal state cannot be reset
messages.explanation: The customer status joins the same batch state. The database preserves terminal outcomes and append-only transition audit events.
messages.durable: submitted / unknown → acknowledged or rejected; audited

flows.name: Inspect operations and audit
flows.note: This small dashboard reads lifecycle counts, queue age, recent batches, attempts and audit records. It is not a full telemetry platform or an administrative mutation UI.

messages.label: Read operational evidence
messages.request:
GET /api/ops/summary
GET /api/ops/batches
GET /api/ops/batches/{id}
Authorization: Bearer <operations token>
messages.request_label: GET lifecycle summary / batches / batch detail
messages.explanation: Operations tokens have a separate role. No customer token can use these endpoints. The page displays actual persisted state.

messages.label: Aggregate lifecycle and bounded details
messages.request: COUNT chargebacks grouped by pending or batch state; COUNT batches by state; oldest unassigned received_at; bounded recent batches, attempts and audit events
messages.response: Counts, age in seconds, manifests with SHA-256 and bytes, attempts and audit events
messages.request_label: SELECT grouped state + age + bounded records
messages.explanation: The queue is visible without introducing a separate metrics service. Audit events link accepted chargebacks to their permanent batch and all delivery attempts.
